title: Keep each TypeScript function's cyclomatic complexity at or below 10

facts.note: Test files and vendored/build directories are excluded from the scan.
Emitted by the existing bun_ts_metrics_detector (the source's realizing validator) for any in-scope function scoring above 10, changed or not; no new observer is required, only consuming its output.

fires: An existing, unchanged non-test .ts/.tsx function of 3+ code lines already scores 11 or more — strict scope has no baseline, so it fires too.
A new or edited non-test .ts/.tsx function of 3+ code lines scores 11 or more (1 + decision keywords + &&/||/?? + ternaries).
A refactor adds branches or boolean operators to a function, pushing it above 10.
doesNotFire: A function with fewer than 3 code lines, however many operators it has.
Functions in test files or vendored/build directories.

given: Any TypeScript/TSX source function (3+ code lines, outside test, vendored and build dirs), whether changed or not
when: its cyclomatic complexity (1 + each if/else if/for/while/do/catch/case, each &&/||/??, each ternary) exceeds 10
then: Restructure it to score at or below 10 by separating decisions into coherent, nameable responsibilities without changing behaviour.
prefer: Diagnose first: group branches by policy/responsibility, separate validation and guards from the core operation, spot repeated compound conditions that are a domain predicate.
Extract a coherent decision or policy into an intention-revealing function.
Replace repeated compound conditions with well-named predicates.
Dispatch table/strategy only for a genuinely stable key-to-behaviour mapping.
Keep the caller's control flow showing the important choices.
avoid: Moving the same branch tree unchanged into a generically named helper.
Indirect data structures or opaque encodings used solely to lower the score.
Scattering one policy across tiny functions whose interaction is harder to follow.
Changing boolean semantics, branch order or fallback behaviour.
unless: Function under 3 code lines (not scored: a two-line arrow is not a complexity problem).
Test file or vendored/build directory (outside the scan).
why: Complexity approximates the test cases needed to pin behaviour; above ~10 paths full coverage stops being written and defects settle in untested paths. The score senses too many decisions in one responsibility; hiding branching only hides the signal.
evidence: bun_ts_metrics_detector reports no COMPLEXITY-CYCLOMATIC-TS-001 finding for the triggering function (the triggering violation is gone).
Existing behaviour and path-focused tests remain green.
Extracted code introduces no new nesting, duplication or length violation, and the refactor introduces no new ATDD Bun violations.
Reviewer confirms the resulting decision boundaries correspond to meaningful responsibilities that are easier to name, test and reason about, rather than a relocated or opaquely encoded branch tree.
verifier_detail: Threshold: complexity <= 10 per function; > 10 is a finding. Applies to every in-scope function, changed or unchanged (no baseline).
Counting: complexity = 1 + each decision point. Decision points: if / else if / for / while / do / catch / case keywords, each && / || / ?? operator, each ternary.
Term decision_point: a construct adding an independent path (the list above).
Term trivial_function: a function under three code lines; skipped/not scored.
Scan excludes test files and vendored/build directories.

Thresholds and counting rule are transcribed from the python-pytest sibling coder.refactor.complexity-cyclomatic-typescript and verified to produce identical numbers; the arithmetic must not drift so a repo switching providers sees the same numbers — only the runner differs (native Bun, no Python interpreter).
